sources.label: Lam
sources.title: Unitary forms for holomorphic vertex operator algebras of central charge 24
sources.role: unitary lattice automorphisms and twisted lattice modules; invariant-form convention
sources.source_status: Published in Letters in Mathematical Physics 113 (2023), article 28, 2 March 2023; cited numbering audited in pinned arXiv v1
results_used: Lemma 2.4, printed pp. 3-4: PCT-conjugate contragredient characterization of invariant sesquilinear forms
Theorem 3.1, printed p. 5: unitarity of positive definite lattice VOAs and ordinary lattice modules
Lemma 3.3, printed pp. 5-6: O(L-hat) preserves the natural positive Hermitian form
Section 3.2 and Lemma 3.8, printed pp. 6-11, statement p. 10: unitarity of the constructed irreducible twisted lattice modules

sources.label: Gui

sources.source_status: Published in Communications in Mathematical Physics 405 (2024), article 72, 4 March 2024; cited numbering audited in pinned final arXiv v2
results_used: Proposition 10.9, printed pp. 60-61: unitarity of all twisted parent modules implies strong unitarity of the rational C2-cofinite fixed algebra
Remark 10.10, printed p. 61: explicit confirmation of applicability to Lam's standard lattice lifts
Proof of Lemma 10.12, equation (10.5), printed p. 62: the PCT-conjugate contragredient transported module action

sources.label: BK
sources.title: Twisted Modules over Lattice Vertex Algebras
sources.role: Twisted lattice defect dimension, fixed-momentum fibers and Fock decomposition
sources.checked_version: arXiv:math/0402315v3, 31 March 2004; 18 pages; internal manuscript date 19 February 2004
sources.source_status: Published as a chapter in Lie Theory and Its Applications in Physics V, World Scientific (2004), pp. 3-26. Numbering here is pinned to arXiv v3.
results_used: Equation (4.53), printed page 16 / PDF page 16: The squared defect dimension is the order of the relevant finite nondegenerate quotient.
Proposition 4.3 and equations (4.54)-(4.55), printed page 16 / PDF page 16: The twisted module is induced from its oscillator-vacuum subspace and has the corresponding symmetric Fock factor.
Lemma 4.7, printed page 17 / PDF page 17: Momentum fibers are translated by projected lattice vectors and carry the irreducible finite defect representation.

Theorem 4.2 and Remark 4.4, printed page 18 / PDF page 18: Classification and explicit Heisenberg-module decomposition S(hat h_sigma^+) tensor e^(lambda_0) C[pi_0 Q] tensor C^d(sigma). The source uses plus for negative-mode creation operators.
sources.scope_check: For the even unimodular lattice and standard lift, the momentum shift is zero. The claim that weight four consists only of the zero-momentum oscillator-vacuum fiber also uses rho_g=4 and positive definiteness. The dimension 2^16 is derived independently from KRR (A.2.5), not asserted for arbitrary unrelated lattices.

sources.label: BDM
sources.title: Twisted Sectors for Tensor Product Vertex Operator Algebras Associated to Permutation Groups
sources.role: Permutation-twisted module construction and swap ground-weight comparison
sources.source_status: Published in Communications in Mathematical Physics 227 (May 2002), 349-384; cited numbering audited in pinned arXiv v2
results_used: Equation (3.6), printed page 14 / PDF page 14: the transformed single-factor conformal field, including its central-charge correction.

Theorem 3.9, printed/PDF pages 22-23, explicit formula on page 23: L_g(0)=L(0)/k+(k^2-1)c/(24k) for the k-cycle-twisted module constructed from a V-module; c is the central charge of one factor V, not of V tensor k.
Theorem 4.4, printed/PDF pages 26-27: equivalence of ordinary V-modules with ordinary k-cycle-twisted tensor-product modules, preserving irreducibility.
sources.scope_check: For a holomorphic CFT-type seed U of charge c_seed, its unique ordinary module has ground weight zero. The swap of U tensor U therefore has twisted ground weight c_seed/16, at least 8 when c_seed is at least 128. The theorem is not restricted to lattice VOAs. It supplies the twisted spectrum; it does not itself assert existence or unitarity of the holomorphic orbifold extension.

sources.label: vEMS
sources.title: Construction and Classification of Holomorphic Vertex Operator Algebras
sources.role: General-central-charge type-zero cyclic holomorphic orbifold theorem and positivity hypotheses
sources.checked_version: arXiv:1507.08142v3, 28 November 2017, 22:35:42 UTC; 37 pages; Section 5 numbering is version-specific
sources.source_status: Published in Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle's Journal) 759 (2020), 61-99; publisher gives online publication date 16 November 2017; cited numbering audited in pinned arXiv v3
results_used: Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed/PDF pages 11-12: rationality and C2-cofiniteness of the cyclic fixed algebra, and its n^2 simple modules W^(i,j) from twisted-sector eigenspaces.
Theorem 5.11 and the following definition, printed/PDF pages 17-18: rho_g lies in (1/n^2)Z and the automorphism type is t=n^2 rho_g modulo n.

Theorem 5.16, printed/PDF pages 20-21: a simple, rational, C2-cofinite, holomorphic CFT-type parent with positive conformal weights for all nonvacuum W^(i,j) admits the isotropic-subgroup extension; H=H^perp gives a holomorphic extension, retaining these finiteness properties and self-contragredience.
Type-zero specialization after Theorem 5.16, printed page 21 / PDF page 21: the compatible labels have fusion group Z_n times Z_n, quadratic form ij/n, and holomorphic extension direct_sum_i W^(i,0).
sources.scope_check: Section 5 applies to general central charge, independently of the later charge-24 classification. Apply it to the parent U tensor U, whose charge is 2*c_seed. BDM gives type 4*rho_swap=c_seed/4 modulo 2, hence zero for c_seed=128*2^k. The antisymmetric untwisted module has positive weight because the unique weight-zero vector is swap-invariant; both twisted eigenspaces have weight at least c_seed/16, so all three nonvacuum fixed-algebra modules satisfy the required positivity. This theorem establishes the strongly rational holomorphic extension, not unitarity; preservation of the primary gap is a separate low-weight argument.
